name: Poly(A) Tail / PABP Competition
therapeuticGoalDescription: Increase or decrease protein synthesis by regulating mRNA translation without altering RNA abundance.
molecularDefect: Diseases in which poly(A)-binding protein association with the target transcript sustains translation and stability that is therapeutically undesirable.
suitableVariantTypes: Not variant-driven. Applies where modulating PABP association with the poly(A) tail changes translation efficiency or transcript stability beneficially.
rnaTargetRegion: The poly(A) site and immediately flanking 3' UTR sequence.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript with a mapped poly(A) site and sufficient flanking 3' UTR sequence for selective targeting.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs: PMO, 2'-MOE full-phosphorothioate, LNA/DNA mixmers
designRules: Steric occupancy only - no RNase H recruitment. PABP binding is distributed across poly(A) tail; competitive ASO must be precisely positioned near poly(A) site.
advantages: Modulates both translation efficiency and mRNA stability simultaneously; targets a well-characterized protein-RNA interface.
limitations: PABP binding is distributed across poly(A) tail; competitive ASO must be precisely positioned near poly(A) site.
offTargetConsiderations: Many mRNAs share poly(A) tail architecture; selectivity depends on flanking 3' UTR sequence specificity.
clinicalTrialExamples: None identified; proof-of-concept in mRNA stability assays.

evidenceLevel.note: Mechanistic basis is clear; preclinical only; no approved therapy.

arbitration.note: Distinct from A11 (APA modulation) which targets poly(A) site selection via splicing; A31 targets PABP binding directly for translation/stability effects.
